Subject: Quick clarifications on billing units for long streaming sessions

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our finance and infra teams around how billing units are applied for our planned long-running inference streams:

- We have bots that maintain 20k-token context windows across sessions (frequent prefix reuse). Do you bill on raw token count, or is there an amortized/conversational bucket applied?
- If a session runs for 10 minutes with many short replies, how does rounding/minimum quantum work? For example, if we send 12 tokens then 3 tokens then 5 tokens, how are those aggregated on the invoice?
- How do prefix/KV cache hits affect metering (are cached prefix tokens credited, partially credited, or ignored)?
- We're considering committing to a 6-month seat bundle if unit economics are favorable. Can you show an example invoice line for a high-KV-reuse workload and how discounts apply versus pure per-token pricing?

I've attached a small sample of our hourly usage from last week (glacier_sample_usage.csv) — rough numbers to ground the example. Procurement is looped for contract constraints.

Appreciate a short worked example we can forward to finance.

Best,
Caroline

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>

Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on billing units for long streaming sessions

Caroline —

Thanks for the usage file and great questions. High level answers up front, followed by a worked example based on your CSV.

Short answers:
- Metering basis: billed tokens = unique active input+output tokens considered per logical session window. We use conversation-window aggregation with an adjustable window (default 30m inactivity).
- Rounding/quantum: tokens are rounded up to an 8-token quantum per aggregation bucket. That means small bursts within the same aggregation bucket get coalesced before rounding.
- KV/prefix caching: we credit repeated prefix tokens when the prefix is cache-hit across the same pinned session; typical credit is 50% of token price for warm KV reuse in committed bundles, 0% in pure on-demand.
- Discounts: commit-based seat bundles provide a multiplier on per-token rates and increase KV crediting from 0% -> 50% (configurable). Seat bundles also give a per-month committed token floor that reduces effective unit price for predictable workloads.

Worked example (from your file — simplified):
- Week sample: 120k generated tokens, 300k input tokens, many repeated prefixes (~40% reuse).
- Aggregation: conversation window groups requests with <30m gap. After aggregation and coalescing, token total that is subject to rounding: 400,000 tokens.
- Quantum rounding: rounded_total = ceil(400,000 / 8) * 8 = 400,000 (no change here, but see microbursts example below).
- KV crediting (if committed seat bundle): 40% reuse -> we apply 50% credit on those 160k reused tokens -> credit = 80k tokens equivalent -> billable tokens = 320k.
- Example rates: on-demand per-token = $0.00030; committed bundle effective = $0.00024 (20% discount).
- Invoice line (monthly): 320,000 billable tokens x $0.00024 = $76.80

Microburst illustration (why quantum matters):
- If you have many tiny calls (12,3,5 tokens) within same aggregation bucket we first sum to 20 and then round to quantum -> ceil(20/8)*8 = 24 tokens billed instead of 12+3+5 = 20 (no change in this case), but with lots of 1–3 token calls the quantum can increase billable by ~10–15% if not batched.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm whether you want the default 30m aggregation window or a shorter 5m window (changes the coalescing and rounding behavior).
2) If you plan to commit, we can run a simulated invoice for the last 3 months of your CSV to show expected spend under both on-demand and a 20% commit discount with seat bundle baseline.

I attached a quick pilot quote PDF and a one-page playbook link. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk finance through the math.

Best,

Caroline —

Appreciate the sample usage. We ran the numbers with the 3-month window in your CSV and here is a concise proposal you can take to finance/procurement:

Proposal summary (Glacier Analytics pilot)
- Pilot length: 3 months (billing monthly)
- Commitment: 3 seats (team access) + 2M committed token floor / month
- Pricing: committed unit price = $0.00024 / billable token (20% off on-demand)
- KV credit: 50% credit on repeated prefix/KV reuse for pinned sessions
- Aggregation window: default 30m (we can enable 5m on request)
- Rounding quantum: 8 tokens per aggregation bucket (visible on invoice line)

Worked monthly math (rounded):
- Raw tokens (input + generated): 420,000
- Post-aggregation coalesced tokens: 400,000
- Reused prefix tokens (40%): 160,000 -> KV credit @50% = 80,000 token credit
- Billable tokens = 320,000 -> meets committed floor (2M) partially; underfloor exposure negotiated as overage at $0.00030 or apply credit against future months.
- Monthly pilot cost = 320,000 * $0.00024 = $76.80 (see caveat on floor coverage)

Caveats and options
- If you prefer tighter billing leakage control for microbursts, select the 5m aggregation window. That typically lowers rounding leakage ~8–12% for workloads with many small RPCs.
- If you want full avoidance of repeated-prefix charge, ask about a higher commitment tier (we can increase KV credit to 70% for a +10% price uplift).

Next steps
1) Confirm aggregation window (30m default or 5m).
2) Confirm whether procurement prefers committed-floor coverage (we can convert the 2M floor into a 6-month amortized credit).
3) If agreed, we will send a formal SOW and pilot DocuSign link.

Happy to take a call this week to walk through the sample invoice line-by-line with your finance team — feel free to propose times.

Regards,
